title: Nuclear Fusion: The Race to Unlimited Clean Energy

slides.heading: Nuclear Fusion
slides.body: The Race to Unlimited Clean Energy

slides.heading: What Is Nuclear Fusion?
slides.body: Fusion is the process that powers the Sun — two light atomic nuclei merge to form a heavier one, releasing enormous amounts of energy. It's the opposite of fission, which splits atoms apart.

slides.heading: Why Fusion Beats Fission
slides.body: Unlike nuclear fission reactors, fusion produces no long-lived radioactive waste and carries no meltdown risk. A fusion reaction simply stops if containment is lost — making it inherently safe.

slides.heading: The Fuel: Seawater & Lithium
slides.body: Fusion reactors use deuterium and tritium — isotopes of hydrogen. Deuterium can be extracted from seawater in virtually limitless quantities, making fusion fuel one of Earth's most abundant resources.

slides.heading: The Big Challenge: 100 Million °C
slides.body: To fuse nuclei, plasma must reach over 100 million degrees Celsius — hotter than the Sun's core. Containing this superheated plasma without any material touching it is the central engineering challenge.

slides.heading: How Tokamaks Contain Plasma
slides.body: The tokamak design uses powerful magnetic fields to trap plasma in a donut-shaped chamber. Superconducting magnets create a magnetic 'bottle' that keeps the plasma away from reactor walls.

slides.heading: ITER: Humanity's Biggest Experiment
slides.body: ITER, under construction in southern France, is a collaboration of 35 nations. When complete, it aims to produce ten times more energy than it consumes — proving fusion is a viable power source.

slides.heading: The Private Sector Joins the Race
slides.body: Startups like Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Helion Energy, and TAE Technologies have attracted billions in funding. They're betting on compact, high-field magnets to reach commercial fusion faster than national programs.

slides.heading: Key Milestones Crossed
slides.body: NIF achieved fusion ignition in 2022, producing more energy than the laser input. High-temperature superconducting magnets have hit new records, and plasma hold times keep improving year after year.

slides.heading: A Star on Earth
slides.body: Fusion promises clean, safe, and nearly limitless energy — potentially ending fossil fuel dependence. The question is no longer if fusion works, but when it will power our homes and cities.
